title: Agent Version Manifest V1
description: What an agent version IS under traigent.content_identity.v1. Identity and version are separate: agent_id is a declared, project-owned, server-minted identity that never changes when the code changes; the agent VERSION is the digest of a build manifest (what was built) and is complemented, per trial, by the provider/model versions actually OBSERVED at run time (what ran). build_digest = 'sha256:' + lowercase hex SHA-256(UTF8('traigent.content_identity.agent_build.v1') || 0x00 || jcs_v1(AgentBuildManifestV1)). It is unkeyed: the manifest carries only digests, revisions and version strings, never prompts or user content. Normative text: docs/identity/content-identity-v1.md. Versions decide comparability, never identity (the rule already stated on optimization_endpoints.json agent_id / artifact_versions). Every string pattern in this file ends with the portable end anchor (?![\s\S]) instead of $: in Python's re (which Python jsonschema uses) $ also matches before a trailing newline, so '^x$' would accept 'x\n' -- a second spelling of one identifier. (?![\s\S]) means end-of-string in both ECMA-262 and Python.

CodeRevisionV1.description: Version-control revision the agent was built from. dirty=true means the working tree differed from the commit, so the commit alone does not reproduce the build; producers MUST then also supply source_digest.

commit.description: Full SHA-1 or SHA-256 git object id; abbreviations are not identities.

language_version.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was closed_enum; contract has no enum/const, so the value is not provably content-free

sdk_version.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was closed_enum; contract has no enum/const, so the value is not provably content-free

AgentBuildManifestV1.description: The build manifest whose jcs_v1 digest is the agent build version. It MUST commit to the full behaviour-affecting surface: code (code_revision and/or source_digest; source_digest REQUIRED when code_revision.dirty is true), asset_digests with ALL THREE categories (prompts, helper_modules, tool_definitions -- an empty map asserts that the category is empty), the candidate configuration (applied_config_digest), and a coverage declaration. coverage='complete' asserts that every behaviour-affecting input is in the manifest; 'partial' admits that something is not (e.g. a helper the SDK could not locate). A partial manifest still yields a build_digest for history and comparison, but is NOT certifiable (CertifiableAgentBuildManifestV1; compute_agent_build_digest(..., certifiable=True)). coverage is a producer declaration: nothing offline can prove completeness. Every field is a digest, a revision or a version string -- no content.

agent_id.description: The project-owned agent identity (Backend agents.id). Part of the manifest so two agents with byte-identical builds still get distinct build digests.

label.x-content-note: INV-GAP S1,S3,S5,O2,H1: not inventoried (free string): label
label.description: Optional human label (e.g. 'v1.3', a release tag). Part of the digest: relabelling is a new version by design, so a label can never be moved onto different bits.

source_digest.description: The SDK's afp2 agent fingerprint (docs/fingerprints/fp2.md) of the callable plus bound state.

dependency_lock_digest.description: SHA-256 of the dependency lock file bytes (uv.lock, poetry.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml) the agent ran under.

asset_digests.description: Digests of every behaviour-affecting file outside the decorated function, keyed by a stable asset name within its category. All three categories are required; {} asserts the category is empty.

propertyNames.x-content-note: INV-GAP S1,S3,S5,O2,H1: not inventoried (free object/array): prompts
INV-GAP S1,S3,S5,O2,H1: not inventoried (free object/array): helper_modules

helper_modules.description: Source files of helper modules the agent imports from the project (not third-party packages, which dependency_lock_digest covers).

propertyNames.x-content-note: INV-GAP S1,S3,S5,O2,H1: not inventoried (free object/array): tool_definitions

tool_definitions.description: Tool / function-calling specifications and retriever definitions.

applied_config_digest.description: fp2 digest of the configuration the agent runs with: the trial's configuration for a candidate, the promoted configuration for a head, the default configuration for a base build (digest of {} when there are no knobs). Required: the configuration is part of what the version is.

coverage.description: Producer's declaration of whether this manifest covers every behaviour-affecting input. Only 'complete' is certifiable.

ObservedProviderVersionV1.description: One provider/model actually observed during a trial, taken from the provider RESPONSE, not from configuration. requested_model is what was asked for; response_model is what the provider says served it (e.g. a dated snapshot behind an alias); system_fingerprint is the provider's backend fingerprint when it returns one. An alias ('gpt-4o', 'claude-latest') is not a version: only response_model / system_fingerprint witness what ran.

provider.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was closed_enum; contract has no enum/const, so the value is not provably content-free

requested_model.x-content-note: INV-GAP S1,S3,S5,O2,H1: not inventoried (free string): requested_model

response_model.x-content-note: INV-GAP S1,S3,S5,O2,H1: not inventoried (free string): response_model
response_model.description: null when the provider response did not name a model: an honest 'unknown', never a copy of requested_model.

system_fingerprint.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was digest; contract has no digest pattern, so the value is not provably content-free

AgentVersionV1.description: An agent version as recorded against a run or a certificate: the identity, the build digest, and (optionally inlined) the manifest it was computed from.

CertifiableAgentBuildManifestV1.description: An AgentBuildManifestV1 that may back a certificate: coverage MUST be 'complete'.

CertifiableAgentVersionV1.description: An AgentVersionV1 that may back a certificate: the manifest MUST be inlined and certifiable, so the issuer can recompute build_digest and check coverage.
